cards.text: God is still giving Moses words to pass on to the Israelites. He's covered servants, oxen, lawsuits and feasts (Exodus 21–23). Now He looks down the road ahead, and He's sending someone out in front of them.

cards.question: Who does God say He's sending ahead of the Israelites?
What does God say the angel will do for the Israelites along the way?

answers.text: Protect them and bring them to the place God prepared
Teach them the laws and settle every one of their disputes
Count the tribes and choose the leaders for each one

cards.text: Then God gives a heads-up about this angel: pay attention to him, listen to his voice, and do not defy him. Friend, this is NOT a GPS you tune out because you "know a shortcut."

cards.question: God says the Israelites must not defy the angel. What reason does He give?

answers.text: He will turn back to Egypt
He will go to another people

cards.question: God says His Name is in the angel He's sending ahead of Israel.

cards.text: Now the flip side. If they listen carefully to the angel's voice and do everything God says, God makes them a promise.

cards.question: If the Israelites listen and obey, what does God promise to do about their enemies?

answers.text: Be an enemy to their enemies

cards.text: If they listen, Israel's enemies will have God as their enemy, and friend, I'd rather pick a fight with a hot oven. Then He names the land His angel is leading them into: the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Six nations live in that land. What does God say He'll do to them?

cards.text: Those nations come with their own gods. And God doesn't leave Israel guessing about what to do with them.

cards.question: God says Israel can follow the nations' practices, as long as they don't bow down to their gods.
Instead of serving the nations' gods, what does God tell Israel to do with them?

answers.text: Demolish them and smash their sacred stones
Leave them standing and stay away from them
Carry them off and keep them as plunder

cards.text: Instead of all that, they're to serve the LORD their God. And His blessing reaches right down to the everyday basics on the table at every meal.

cards.question: When they serve Him, God says He will bless their ___ and their ___.
Along with blessing the everyday basics, God promises to take away sickness from among them.

cards.text: God keeps going: no woman in their land will miscarry or be barren, and He says, 'I will fulfill the number of your days.' Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer counting falling dust, so a full count of days from God sounds AMAZING to me.
Before Israel even arrives, God says He'll send His terror ahead of them. He'll throw into confusion every nation they meet.

cards.question: When God's terror reaches Israel's enemies, what does God say they'll do?

cards.text: That's not the only thing God sends on ahead. The next one is a whole lot smaller.

cards.question: What does God send before Israel to drive the Hivites, Canaanites and Hittites out of the way?

cards.text: The HORNET! One hornet buzzes into my bakery and I'm diving behind the oven, gold base and all.
But here's the twist: God says He won't drive the nations out in a single year. It has to do with what would happen to the land if it emptied out all at once.

cards.question: God won't drive the nations out of the land in a single year. Why not?

answers.text: The land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply
Israel would not be ready to fight every battle in one year
The nations would band together and attack Israel all at once

cards.question: So God will drive them out little by little, until Israel becomes ___ and possesses the land.

cards.text: Then God sketches the borders: from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. Friend, my whole territory used to be the back of a takeout menu in a junk drawer.

cards.question: God says He will deliver the land's inhabitants into Israel's hand, and Israel will drive them out.

cards.text: Now God gets to one last warning. It's about how Israel deals with these nations and their gods.

cards.question: Israel may make a covenant with these nations, as long as it doesn't include their gods.
God says these nations must not remain in Israel's land. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They would cause Israel to sin against Him
They would take the best fields for themselves
They would grow and outnumber the Israelites

cards.text: And God ends with this: 'For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.' It's like opening one group chat "real quick" and looking up an hour later.
